_comment: Independent, requirements-derived access-control policy oracle for the
HRBAC manuscript, added in response to a reviewer premortem: a permission
table or test suite generated from roles.go cannot validate roles.go,
because a defect shared between the implementation and its own
self-description would not appear as a failure. This file is authored
from the manuscript's stakeholder requirements (Introduction and
Section 'Access-control design') without reference to either
reviewed as an independent document before being used to score either
GetEffectivePermissions() against every cell; it fails against the
historical chaincode/hrbac hierarchy (confirmed by a throwaway copy of
the same test run against that package during development, the same
requirements_basis: Farmers need operational control (write sensor data, actuate zone
Agronomists need history but no actuation rights: zone-scoped read
access and the ability to issue cross-zone tokens, not ControlZone.
Certification bodies need compliance evidence (audit records) without
visibility into raw zone sensor data or actuation.
Supply-chain partners need provenance (their own records) but not
Sensors and gateways are device-tier roles: sensors only write;
gateways read and control their own zone as the sensors' registration
hierarchy_note: The intended hierarchy is not the single chain SupplyChain-Certifier-
originally displayed: that total order is exactly what makes the
auditor-separation defect possible, since it forces Certifier's grants
to be inherited by everything above it. The intended structure is a
branch at SupplyChain: one branch is Certifier alone (audit), the
other is Agronomist then Farmer (operations), both merging only at
Admin. The matrix below is this branching structure's transitive
closure, independent of how any chaincode file happens to implement
Symmetrically for the device chain, Gateway inherits Sensor's
WriteSensor (a gateway is a superset of the sensor it registers), so
Gateway's row includes WriteSensor even though it is not Gateway's
